messages:
Maya (People Ops): thanks all — creating this thread for follow-ups from today’s town hall re: reviews/leveling/promos. leave short Qs and we’ll answer or escalate.
Chris (Senior IC): quick Q — if my promotion is approved in the middle of a pay period, when does salary change kick in?
Maya (People Ops): good Q. standard is effective first day of next pay period after approval. we can do retro pay in exceptions — backpay usually to the approved promotion date. ping @Jenna if you think you need retroactive. :sparkles:
Raj (Engineering Manager): also — what level of detail do managers need in the promo packet now? saw the new template but want to confirm minimum fields.
Jenna (People Ops): we streamlined the packet: 1) short impact summary (3 bullets) 2) examples of scope change 3) manager calibration note 4) proposed comp. link: https://intranet.redwood/peopleops/promo-packet. minimal is the three bullets + manager note.
Lina (VP Eng): adding — include 1-2 measurable outcomes where possible. calibration panels prefer concrete examples.
Chris (Senior IC): thanks. another: does the leveling exception path exist for ICs who do cross-functional scope, or is that manager-only?
Maya (People Ops): exceptions can be submitted by managers or by staff with manager support. we review on a rolling basis; give 2 weeks for initial review. if it’s cross-functional, include stakeholder feedback in the packet.
Anya (Recruiting): hiring/offer question — if someone joins during promo window, are they eligible for the current cycle?
Jenna (People Ops): new hires are eligible for leveling review after 6 months, except in rare near-term exceptions approved by People Ops + hiring manager. offers should not promise immediate promo.
Tom (CEO): one quick reminder — promotions should align with role clarity. managers: ping me or Lina if a case looks org-shifting.
Raj (Engineering Manager): benefits Q from my team — is the 401k match schedule changing this year?
Maya (People Ops): no change to match schedule for this cycle. any future changes will be communicated 60 days ahead.
Chris (Senior IC): parental leave follow-up — did we confirm duration for birth vs adoption?
Jenna (People Ops): policy remains: 16 weeks primary caregiver (birth) and 12 weeks secondary/adoption. still paid — see benefits portal for details.
Chris (Senior IC): thanks.
Maya (People Ops): timeline recap for promos we covered today:
```
- Promo nominations open: 2026-04-01
- Manager packet deadline: 2026-04-21
- Calibration panels: 2026-04-28 to 2026-05-05
- Notifications: by 2026-05-12
```
Maya (People Ops): if you need an exception to any date, file the form and tag @Jenna. we’ll triage. also leaving a tiny checklist for managers: 1) update role doc 2) collect 2-3 examples 3) submit packet 4) note proposed comp.
Chris (Senior IC): are salary bands being published this quarter? could help managers justify ranges in the packet.
Maya (People Ops): yes — band refresh is scheduled for next week, will post to the handbook and link in this thread when live.
Raj (Engineering Manager): can we get a short office-hours slot for managers to run through tricky cases?
Lina (VP Eng): I can do a 30-min slot after calibration opens, happy to join.
Maya (People Ops): perfect — scheduling manager office hours: 2026-04-22 1600 PST. invite will go out.
hr-bot: Reminder: review docs updated by People Ops — https://intranet.redwood/peopleops/review-process (auto).
Maya (People Ops): thanks everyone — we’ll keep answers short here. if you have private comp questions DM me or @Jenna. we’ll follow up on any outstanding asks in this thread and pin a final FAQ. :memo:
